prompts.cover:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: finished short-story book cover for White Thunder. Generate a portrait 9:16 image, exactly 864 by 1536 pixels if possible. Render the exact title "White Thunder" ONCE, large and beautifully legible at the top, classic restrained serif typography integrated into the painting; no other words.

A buoyant, tactile fantasy winter sporting novel cover in Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil painting: broad rhythmic colour and value shapes, varied opaque directional brushwork, quieter connecting passages, selective impasto, connected shadows and lost edges. Avoid glossy digital faces, uniform bevelled strokes and theatrical rim light. Pale winter sun, ivory snow, muted violet-blue shadows, charcoal woodland and subdued mulberry; natural motivated light rather than automatic orange-blue contrast.

Central scene: a colossal carved SNOW HARE with narrow head, proud chest, exquisitely incised snow-fur grooves and two very tall intact ears, one early glorious racing bound on a frozen palace lake. This is sculpted packed snow, not a furry living mammal. Its full body and four coherent legs read clearly, powerful folded haunches, long hind feet. Its two ears rise roughly a person's height above the woman riding it. Rilka is a 39-year-old adult toy carver, warm medium-brown complexion, wind-reddened cheeks, dark brown curly hair with a few grey threads, sturdy ordinary build, a practical dark winter riding coat, brown gloves and boots, and a magnificent mulberry wool cape streaming behind her. She sits on a simple saddle at the shoulders, leans into the motion with BOTH gloved hands pressed to the hare's packed-snow shoulders; her hands supply its movement. No reins, bridle, weapons or glowing eyes. Her expression is delighted and fiercely competitive.

Compose a striking single silhouette and diagonal motion with generous quiet sky above for the exact title, tiny spectators and palace terraces only as a distant winter suggestion. The image represents the early race, before the hare's ears are sacrificed. Invite the sporting delight of the story, with no plot-summary montage. All-ages, no injury or horror.
prompts.character_sheet:
Use case: identity-preserve. Transform the attached inspected White Thunder cover into a finished LANDSCAPE CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET, 1536 by 1024 pixels, for the SAME woman Rilka. Treat the cover as the identity, clothing, colour and oil-brushwork reference. Preserve her adult age (39), medium-brown complexion, wind-red cheeks, dark curly hair with grey threads especially at the temples, dark brows, ordinary sturdy build, joyous/competitive personality. Preserve the dark blue winter riding coat, brown gloves, laced brown knee-high boots and mulberry wool cape with pale collar. No armour, weapons, wand, crown or new scars. Keep her recognisably the same woman in every view.

Use a warm off-white quiet canvas background with clear readable organisation. On the left two-thirds: THREE full-body studies, front three-quarter view, true profile view, and back view, with consistent scale, outfit layers, cape length and boots. On the right: three larger face/expression studies, concentrated determination, delighted open laughter matching the cover, and alarm at an awkward landing. Small lower-right prop studies: a palm-sized finely carved white snow rabbit, and the Winter Cup, a broad silver soup-tureen-sized trophy with TWO curling handles, a lid and snowflake finial. The cup is a physical vessel, not a crown or shield.

Labels, clearly readable, exactly: main header "Rilka", story subtitle "White Thunder"; modest study labels "Front", "Profile", "Back", "Determination", "Delight", "Alarm", "Snow rabbit", "Winter Cup". No paragraphs or duplicated headers. Maintain painterly Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil handling, directional opaque strokes and quieter connecting passages, coherent anatomy, no glossy face or photoreal collage. A reference sheet with multiple complete views, not a scene portrait. The background palace and giant hare from the cover must give way to this sheet layout.
prompts.location_original:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: landscape location reference oil painting for the finished short story White Thunder. Generate 1536 by 1024 landscape, no text or lettering.

Paint the Seven Steps course of the Ice Kingdom's Great Winter Contest, in daylight winter sun. View from a raised finish landing near the frozen palace lake, looking UP the snow-covered palace hillside. A palace sits above seven snow-covered terraced ledges. The straight central descent has grown-person-high vertical faces and short horizontal landing shelves, making a steep white stairway. Across the wide palace frontage, broad ramps zigzag alternately left and right between those same terraces, giving long-legged snow mounts room to gallop. The contrast of short direct drops and long smooth ramps must be visibly intelligible. At the lowest lip a clearly bounded gap of about twenty feet opens above the frozen lake; a deep rope catch-net hangs beneath it between sturdy posts. On the near, raised finish landing stand TWO red finish poles. Tiny warmly clothed spectators on banks and grandstands, a few cloth pennants, sparse winter trees including an old leafless willow to one side. The course dominates, not an enormous generic ice citadel. No racers or large foreground people needed.

Canadian Group of Seven inspired opaque oil painting, simplified but coherent architecture and spatial planes, varied directional paint, substantial impasto only selectively, quieter connected snow passages, natural ivory light and muted violet/slate shadows with dark tree masses. Keep shadows connected and allow lost edges. No glossy fantasy rendering, automatic orange-blue split or decorative glowing magic. Paint a place where a real peculiar sporting event could be watched.
prompts.location_snow_correction:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the attached inspected ORIGINAL Seven Steps location oil painting. Preserve the lovely winter light, oil brushwork, distant palace, trees, crowds, wide alternating left-right galloping ramps and TWO red finish poles. Correct the CENTRAL COURSE GEOMETRY so it matches the story White Thunder.

The centre currently resembles a frozen waterfall. Replace that centre with seven dry, matte packed-snow racing ledges, like a broad snow-bank stairway: grown-person-high near-vertical SNOW faces, SHORT FLAT landing shelves barely a giant crouched hare's body length, and a direct descent broad enough for two racing mounts beside each other. The faces are cut banks of white snow with rough packed texture, NOT frozen flowing cascades, icicles, channels or water infrastructure. The longer broad ramps keep sweeping left and right across the whole palace frontage between these same ledges; preserve their conspicuous extra distance.

At the lowest lip, make the last jump and its safety arrangement clear: the course's far raised lip and the near raised finish landing are separated by a roughly twenty-foot open horizontal gap, with frozen blue palace lake LOWER beneath them. The existing rope catch-net should read as a deep sagging HAMMOCK BELOW that flight path, secured to strong posts at its sides, not a vertical barrier across the racing line. Keep the two red poles on the raised NEAR finish landing beyond the gap. No racing figures, labels, diagrams or text. Keep the same coherent daylight winter oil-painting composition. This is one targeted correction of the race course, retaining the original painting's mood and setting.
prompts.location_finish_correction:
Edit only the FOREGROUND FINISH ARRANGEMENT of this inspected Seven Steps oil painting. Preserve the palace, seven dry packed-snow stair ledges, alternating ramps, light, brushwork, trees and crowds exactly as established.

The broad flat icy foreground makes the jump's near landing ambiguous. Make a clearly RAISED SNOW-COVERED NEAR FINISH PLATFORM extending from the bottom of the painting into the scene, with a visible rear-facing snow/stone edge across the image just behind the TWO red finish poles. Both red poles stand on this same raised platform. That near edge stops a SHORT distance, about twenty feet in world scale, before the far course's lowest raised lip. Between these TWO visibly raised edges there is a bounded OPEN HORIZONTAL JUMP GAP, and frozen blue lake is visibly lower below it.

The catch-net sits deep DOWN in that bounded gap, a sagging horizontal rope hammock visibly attached between the banks/side posts and below the line a jumping animal would take. It must not look like a vertical fence at the end of the course. Give a slightly oblique view of the net so its depth is readable. Keep the central racing path pointing from the snow steps across the short gap to the near platform BETWEEN the red poles. No new structures, racers, text, flowing water, arrows or diagram labels. Retain the painting's harmonious winter mood. This is a small spatial clarification of the final leap; the beautiful rest of the location remains.
